acropoli: Athens' sacred rock, with the 5th-century BC Parthenon at the top, the Erechtheion temple with the Caryatid statues and the Propylaea at the entrance. From the top you see the whole city down to the sea.
museoac: The museum holding the original sculptures, friezes and statues of the Acropolis, in a modern glass building built over ancient excavations. The Parthenon Gallery on the top floor has the friezes arranged as on the temple, with a view of the rock.
plaka: The oldest quarter, at the foot of the rock: lanes of neoclassical houses, bougainvillea and tavernas. Above, Anafiotika looks like a Cycladic village, with little white houses built in the 19th century by workers from the island of Anafi.
agora: Ancient Agora and the Temple of Hephaestus

The centre of civic life in ancient Athens, where Socrates and Demosthenes walked: the 5th-century BC Temple of Hephaestus, the best preserved in all Greece, the rebuilt Stoa of Attalos, which houses the museum, and the Byzantine Church of the Holy Apostles.
romana: Roman Agora, Tower of the Winds and Hadrian's Library

The market of Roman Athens, with the Tower of the Winds, a 1st-century BC octagonal building that was a water clock and sundial. Close by, next to Monastiraki Square, are the remains of Hadrian's Library.
zeus: Temple of Olympian Zeus and Hadrian's Arch

Fifteen 17-metre Corinthian columns, all that's left of Greece's largest temple, built over 600 years and completed by Emperor Hadrian. Next to it, Hadrian's Arch marks the boundary between Greek and Roman Athens.
stadio: The all-white marble stadium where the first modern Olympics were held in 1896. You can climb to the winners' podium and walk through the athletes' tunnel, with an audio guide included in the ticket.
syntagma: Syntagma Square, Parliament and National Garden

In front of Parliament, the Evzones, soldiers in white kilts and pompom shoes, guard the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Right behind the building is the National Garden, with trees and ponds, and at the far end the Zappeion.
museoarch: Greece's most important museum: the gold mask of Agamemnon from Mycenae, the bronze statue of Poseidon (or Zeus), the archaic kouroi, the finds from Santorini and the Antikythera mechanism, a two-thousand-year-old astronomical calculator.
filopappo: A wooded hill opposite the Acropolis, with a Roman monument at the top. The best spot to photograph the Parthenon from across the valley, especially at sunset.
licabetto: The highest hill in the centre (277 metres), with the white chapel of St George at the top: from there you see all of Athens, with the Acropolis and the sea beyond.
